title: Chain-map representatives of affine strictly perfect derived arrows
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $U$ an affine open, and $A^\bullet,B^\bullet$ strictly perfect complexes of $\mathcal O_U$-modules [def-pc-perfect-complex]. For every arrow $f:Q(A^\bullet)\to Q(B^\bullet)$ in $D(\mathcal O_U)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], there is a chain map $\alpha:A^\bullet\to B^\bullet$ such that $Q(\alpha)=f$.

proof.text: Transport the localized site to the affine scheme $U\cong\operatorname{Spec}(R)$. Each term of the transported $A^\bullet$ and $B^\bullet$ is a retract of a finite free sheaf, hence quasi-coherent. The affine tilde/global-sections adjunction [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction] recovers these terms by its counit. Taking sections termwise constructs bounded complexes $P^\bullet,Q^\bullet$ of finite projective $R$-modules: map the finite-free retract equations to sections. The counit is natural in the differentials, hence yields actual complex isomorphisms $\widetilde P\cong A$ and $\widetilde Q\cong B$.

Conjugate $f$ by these complex isomorphisms. The factorization isomorphism of [lem-pc-affine-qcoh-derived-equivalence] identifies the resulting arrow with an arrow between the images of $Q(P)$ and $Q(Q)$ in the full quasi-coherent derived subcategory. Its fully faithful inclusion and the equivalence lift the arrow to $D(R)$. By [lem-pc-ring-derived-map-representative], since $P$ is bounded above and projective, this lift has a chain-map representative $\beta:P\to Q$.

Sheafify $\beta$ termwise, conjugate by the complex counit isomorphisms, and transport back to the localized site. Naturality of the factorization isomorphism for the affine equivalence shows that the image of this chain map under $Q$ is the original $f$. This proof uses actual complexes of sections; it chooses no object from an undetermined existence theorem. In the empty affine case all objects and arrows vanish.
